Name: Neel Kumar
Question: Why do liberals hate masculine men so much?
Answer: My great-grandfather was the first high commissioner (aka ambassador) from India to Pakistan. He was in Lahore (then capital of Pakistan) at the time of Indian/Pakistani independence. He was roped into many refugee crises and what I have read from his diaries, they were quite bad. One time a crowd of people who wanted to move to India got frustrated with the glacial pace and essentially had a riot in front of the embassy. My g-grandpa stepped out, unarmed and unaccompanied and, in a very loud voice, said something to the effect of “do you seriously think I want to see your unclean faces every day?” That is a masculine man. And a liberal. He did not need to cower under a desk. He did not even need a gun or a sword or a knife or even a stick. His voice was enough to defuse the anger and frustration and get the situation under control.

Question: Do you agree that “Not to vote IS to vote.”?
Answer: My father would often say “Not deciding is ALSO a decision.” I had no idea he was channeling Harvey Cox. But this used to infuriate me because on many occasions I would have to wait for him to decide. Then, one time I was cooking and asked him “Do you want X or Y?” When he didn’t reply, I asked him if he was going with a non-decision, he said yes. So, I took out the last slice of bread, the last egg and the last remnants of cheese and made myself a sandwich and didn’t cook either X or Y. My dad ended up going to bed hungry. Somehow, his decisions became a whole lot faster after that. :) In 2016, after Trump was declared president-elect, there were many rallies denouncing him. And many of the attendees hadn’t voted. I told my wife “They had their chance just a few days ago and now they are wailing.”

Question: Is there a higher court than the U.S. Supreme Court for appeals?
Answer: Despite what others say, in certain cases there is a higher court. The US has signed various treaties with other countries. Some of those treaties have an associated legal framework and those judges can override the SCOTUS on matters that fall under their authority. For example, the WTO courts.

Question: What factors contribute to the faster speed of roads in Germany compared to the UK?
Answer: Training. In Germany, to get a drivers license, one needs to complete many hundreds of hours of driver training. Certain regions require many tens of hours of experience driving in the snow as well. Getting a drivers license is a serious financial commitment and, as a result, many decide to forego driving and use the extensive public transit. In the US, many people get a drivers license with a mere 5 hours of experience. And it shows.
